lines.text: Nine at the beginning: Its subject meets with his mate. Though they are both of the same character, there will be no error. Advance will call forth approval.

Six in the second place: Its subject is surrounded by screens so large and thick that at midday he can see from them the constellation of the Bushel. If he go and try to enlighten his ruler who is thus emblemed, he will make himself to be viewed with suspicion and dislike. Let him cherish his feeling of sincere devotion that he may thereby move his ruler's mind, and there will be good fortune.

Nine in the third place: Its subject has an additional screen of a large and thick banner, through which at midday he can see the small Mei star. In the darkness he breaks his right arm; but there will be no error.

Nine in the fourth place: Its subject is in a tent so large and thick that at midday he can see from it the constellation of the Bushel. But he meets with the subject of the first line, undivided like himself. There will be good fortune.
Six in the fifth place: Its subject brings around him the men of brilliant ability. There will be occasion for congratulation and praise. There will be good fortune.

Six at the top: Its subject has his house made large, but it only serves as a screen to his household. When he looks at his door, it is still, and there is nobody about it. For three years no one is to be seen. There will be evil.

hexagrams.name: The Traveller
hexagrams.judgment: The Stranger intimates that, in the condition which it denotes, there may be some little attainment and progress. If the stranger or traveller be firm and correct as he ought to be, there will be good fortune.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing a mountain and above it that for fire form the hexagram of the Stranger. The superior man, in accordance with this, exerts his wisdom and caution in the use of punishments and in not allowing litigations to continue.

lines.text: Six at the beginning: The stranger is mean and meanly occupied. It is thus that he brings on himself further calamity.
Six in the second place: The stranger occupies his lodging-house, carrying with him his means of livelihood, and provided with good and trusty servants.
Nine in the third place: The stranger burns his lodging-house, and has lost his servants. However firm and correct he try to be, he will be in peril.
Nine in the fourth place: The traveller is in a resting-place, having also the means of livelihood and the axe, but still saying, 'I am not at ease in my mind.'
Six in the fifth place: Its subject is shooting a pheasant. He will lose his arrow, but in the end he will obtain praise and a high charge.

Nine at the top: It suggests the idea of a bird burning its nest. The stranger, thus represented, first laughs and then cries out. He has lost his ox-like docility too readily and easily. There will be evil.

hexagrams.name: Penetration
hexagrams.judgment: Penetration intimates that, under the conditions which it denotes, there will be some little attainment and progress. There will be advantage in movement onward in whatever direction. It will be advantageous also to see the great man.
hexagrams.image: Two trigrams representing wind, following each other, form the hexagram of Penetration. The superior man, in accordance with this, reiterates his orders, and secures the practice of his affairs.

lines.text: Six at the beginning: Its subject is now advancing, now receding. It would be advantageous for him to have the firm correctness of a brave soldier.
Nine in the second place: The representative of penetration is beneath a couch, and employs diviners and exorcists in a way bordering on confusion. There will be good fortune and no error.
Nine in the third place: Its subject penetrates only by violent and repeated efforts. There will be occasion for regret.
Six in the fourth place: All occasion for repentance in its subject has passed away. He takes game for its threefold use in his hunting.

Nine in the fifth place: With firm correctness there will be good fortune to its subject. All occasion for repentance will disappear, and all his movements will be advantageous. There may have been no good beginning, but there will be a good end. Three days before making any changes, let him give notice of them; and three days after, let him reconsider them. There will thus be good fortune.
Nine at the top: The representative of penetration is beneath a couch, and has lost the axe with which he executed his decisions. However firm and correct he may try to be, there will be evil.

hexagrams.name: Pleasure
hexagrams.judgment: Pleasure intimates that, under its conditions, there will be progress and attainment. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: Two symbols representing the waters of a marsh, one over the other, form the hexagram of Pleasure. The superior man, in accordance with this, encourages the conversation of friends and the stimulus of their common practice.

lines.text: Nine at the beginning: It shows the pleasure of inward harmony. There will be good fortune.
Nine in the second place: It shows the pleasure arising from inward sincerity. There will be good fortune. Occasion for repentance will disappear.
Six in the third place: Its subject brings round himself whatever can give pleasure. There will be evil.
Nine in the fourth place: Its subject is deliberating about what to seek his pleasure in, and is not at rest. He borders on what would be injurious, but there will be cause for joy.
Nine in the fifth place: Its subject is trusting in one who would injure him. The situation is perilous.
Six at the top: It shows the pleasure of its subject in leading and attracting others.

hexagrams.name: Dispersion
hexagrams.judgment: Dispersion intimates that, under its conditions, there will be progress and success. The king goes to his ancestral temple; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing water and that for wind moving above the water form the hexagram of Dispersion. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, presented offerings to God and established the ancestral temple.

lines.text: Six at the beginning: Its subject is engaged in rescuing from the impending evil, and has the assistance of a strong horse. There will be good fortune.
Nine in the second place: Amid the dispersion, its subject hurries to his contrivance for security. All occasion for repentance will disappear.
Six in the third place: Its subject discards any regard to his own person. There will be no occasion for repentance.

Six in the fourth place: Its subject scatters the different parties in the state, which leads to great good fortune. From the dispersion he collects again good men standing out, a crowd like a mound, which is what ordinary men would not have thought of.

Nine in the fifth place: Amidst the dispersion, its subject issues his great announcements as the perspiration flows from his body. He scatters abroad also the accumulations in the royal granaries. There will be no error.
Nine at the top: Its subject disposes of what may be called its bloody wounds, and goes and separates himself from its anxious fears. There will be no error.

hexagrams.name: Regulation
hexagrams.judgment: Regulation intimates that, under its conditions, there will be progress and attainment. But if the regulations which it prescribes be severe and difficult, they cannot be permanent.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing a lake, and above it that for water, form the hexagram of Regulation. The superior man, in accordance with this, constructs his methods of numbering and measurement, and discusses points of virtue and conduct.

lines.text: Nine at the beginning: Its subject does not quit the courtyard outside his door. There will be no error.
Nine in the second place: Its subject does not quit the courtyard inside his gate. There will be evil.
Six in the third place: Its subject shows no appearance of observing the proper regulations, in which case we shall see him lamenting. But there will be no one to blame but himself.
Six in the fourth place: Its subject is quietly and naturally attentive to all regulations. There will be progress and success.
Nine in the fifth place: Its subject is sweetly and acceptably enacting his regulations. There will be good fortune. The onward progress with them will afford ground for admiration.

Six at the top: Its subject is enacting regulations severe and difficult. Even with firmness and correctness there will be evil. But though there will be cause for repentance, it will by and by disappear.

hexagrams.name: Inmost Sincerity
hexagrams.judgment: Inmost sincerity moves even pigs and fish, and leads to good fortune. There will be advantage in crossing the great stream. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing the waters of a marsh and that for wind above it form the hexagram of Inmost Sincerity. The superior man, in accordance with this, deliberates about cases of litigation and delays the infliction of death.

lines.text: Nine at the beginning: Its subject is resting in himself. There will be good fortune. If he sought to any other, he would not find rest.

Nine in the second place: Its subject is like the crane crying out in her hidden retirement, and her young ones responding to her. It is as if it were said, 'I have a cup of good spirits,' and the response were, 'I will partake of it with you.'
Six in the third place: Its subject has met with his mate. Now he beats his drum, and now he leaves off. Now he weeps, and now he sings.
Six in the fourth place: Its subject is like the moon nearly full, and like a horse in a chariot whose fellow disappears. There will be no error.
Nine in the fifth place: Its subject is perfectly sincere, and links others to him in closest union. There will be no error.
Nine at the top: Its subject is like chanticleer trying to mount to heaven. Even with firm correctness there will be evil.

hexagrams.name: Small Excess
hexagrams.judgment: Small excess indicates that, in the circumstances which it implies, there will be progress and attainment. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. What the name denotes may be done in small affairs, but not in great affairs. It is like the notes that come down from a bird on the wing: to descend is better than to ascend. There will in this way be great good fortune.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing a hill and that for thunder above it form the hexagram of Small Excess. The superior man, in accordance with this, in his conduct exceeds in humility, in mourning exceeds in sorrow, and in his expenditure exceeds in economy.

lines.text: Six at the beginning: It suggests the idea of a bird flying, and ascending till the issue is evil.
Six in the second place: Its subject passes by his grandfather, and meets with his grandmother; not attempting anything against his ruler, but meeting him as his minister. There will be no error.
Nine in the third place: Its subject takes no extraordinary precautions against danger, and some in consequence find opportunity to assail and injure him. There will be evil.

Nine in the fourth place: Its subject falls into no error, but meets the exigency of his situation without exceeding in his natural course. If he go forward, there will be peril, and he must be cautious. There is no occasion to be using firmness perpetually.
Six in the fifth place: It suggests the idea of dense clouds, but no rain, coming from our borders in the west. It also shows the prince shooting his arrow, and taking the bird in a cave.

Six at the top: Its subject does not meet the exigency of his situation, and exceeds his proper course. It suggests the idea of a bird flying far aloft. There will be evil. The case is what is called one of calamity and self-produced injury.

hexagrams.name: Completion
hexagrams.judgment: Completion intimates progress and success in small matters. There will be advantage in being firm and correct. There has been good fortune in the beginning; there may be disorder in the end.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing fire and that for water above it form the hexagram of Completion. The superior man, in accordance with this, thinks of evil that may come, and beforehand guards against it.

lines.text: Nine at the beginning: Its subject is like a driver who drags back his wheel, or like a fox which has wet his tail. There will be no error.
Six in the second place: Its subject is like a wife who has lost her carriage-screen. There is no occasion to go in pursuit of it. In seven days she will find it.
Nine in the third place: It suggests the case of Kao Tsung, who attacked the Demon region, but was three years in subduing it. Small men should not be employed in such enterprises.
Six in the fourth place: Its subject has rags provided against any leak in his boat, and is on his guard all day long.

Nine in the fifth place: Its subject is like the neighbour in the east who slaughters an ox for his sacrifice; but this is not equal to the small spring sacrifice of the neighbour in the west, whose sincerity receives the blessing.
Six at the top: Its subject has even his head immersed. The position is perilous.

hexagrams.name: Before Completion
hexagrams.judgment: The state before completion intimates progress and success in the circumstances which it implies. We see a young fox that has nearly crossed the stream, when its tail gets immersed. There will be no advantage in any way.
hexagrams.image: The trigram representing water and that for fire above it form the hexagram of things not yet completed. The superior man, in accordance with this, carefully discriminates among the qualities of things, and the different positions they naturally occupy.

lines.text: Six at the beginning: Its subject is like a fox whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.
Nine in the second place: Its subject drags back his carriage-wheel. With firmness and correctness there will be good fortune.
Six in the third place: With the state of things not yet remedied, its subject advances on, which will lead to evil. But there will be advantage in trying to cross the great stream.

Nine in the fourth place: By firm correctness its subject obtains good fortune, so that all occasion for repentance disappears. Let him stir himself up, as if he were invading the Demon region, where for three years rewards will come to him and his troops from the great kingdom.

Six in the fifth place: By firm correctness its subject obtains good fortune, and has no occasion for repentance. We see in him the brightness of a superior man, and the possession of sincerity. There will be good fortune.

Nine at the top: Its subject is full of confidence and therefore feasting quietly. There will be no error. If he cherish this confidence till he is like the fox who gets his head immersed, it will fail of what is right.
